title: Chaos scenarios for passive-region promotion and latency-budget testing
creator: Riley Chen
description:
Goal: Validate active-passive promotion safety and graceful degradation under realistic failure modes while exercising SLO detection, circuit-breaker behavior, and progressive load-shedding.

Scope: staged chaos scenarios that simulate (A) regional control-plane loss, (B) slow KV store reconvergence, (C) backend GPU pool capacity tax, and (D) API gateway partial network blackholes. Each scenario must include automated/manual failover steps, backup/restore validation, and success criteria for SLO, data integrity, and rollback.

Success criteria (acceptance):
- Promotion time from passive->active < 90s end-to-end for control-plane routing and < 3x median latency for requests in-flight.
- No more than 0.1% user-visible correctness regressions (rerun canonical prompt set).
- KV-store divergence detected and reconciled with automated auditor within 15 minutes; run accepted when divergence <= 0.01%.
- Circuit-breaker and rate-limiter policies engage progressively and maintain error-budget burn rate under 1.5x expected when traffic is shed.
- Backup restore validation passes: snapshot validation checksum and sample query results match production baseline for 99.99% of keys.
- Post-dr checklist completed and signed off by SRE, Runtime Eng, and PM.

Planned artifacts and links:
- Runbook draft: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/RELIABILITY/chaos-passive-promo-runbook
- KV-auditor prototype: https://github.com/redwood-inference/tools/PR-106
- Dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.com/d/DR/active-passive-drill
- Postmortem template: https://docs.redwood.com/pm-templates/drill-postmortem

Planned tests (high level):
1) Controlled passive promotion (no traffic shift): simulate control-plane loss in primary region; promote passive region routing; validate control-plane + data-plane reconnection and KV audit.
2) In-flight tail-latency tax: start synthetic traffic (50% production QPS) and inject 200-500ms tail latency on primary service to observe graceful circuit-breaker open and failover to passive.
3) Progressive rate-limit stress: apply incremental ingress QPS spikes while enabling hierarchical rate-limit tiers; verify shedding order (lowest-priority tenants -> non-critical routes -> best-effort tokens).
4) Backup restore smoke: take incremental snapshot, restore into isolated cluster, run canonical eval set and checksum audit.

Playbook excerpt (step-by-step for scenario 2 - in-flight tail-latency):
- Preconditions: alerting active, DR run coordinator on-call, KV snapshot taken t0.
- Step 0: Mark drill window in Console and disable auto-escalation to PagerDuty for the run.
- Step 1: Route 50% synthetic traffic from load generator to primary region.
- Step 2: Inject latency via netem on subset of backend nodes (controlled CIDR).
- Step 3: Observe circuit-breaker metrics: open_rate, open_duration, reject_count.
- Step 4: If open_rate > 10% and sustained for 30s, trigger canary promotion of passive region (automated) and enable read-only fallback for best-effort routes.
- Step 5: Run KV-auditor to identify asymmetric KV writes; if divergence > 0.01% pause write-promotion and run incremental reconciliation.
- Rollback: If passive region promotion increases user-error rate > 0.5% for 3 minutes, revert routing using staged canary fence and re-route remaining traffic back to primary.

Observability and measurement plan:
- Metrics to capture: request latency p50/p95/p99, error-rate (4xx/5xx), circuit_breaker.opened_count, rate_limiter.shed_count, kv_audit.divergent_keys, promotion_time_seconds, snapshot_restore_time_seconds, error_budget_burn.
- Dashboards: DR drill dashboard (links above) with pre-built panels for each metric and a live check for automated acceptance criteria.
- SLO tie-ins: tests must exercise SLO alarms (runtime SLOs) and validate that alert-runbook actions were appropriate (e.g., traffic routing, rate-limiter adjustments).

Safety and blast-radius controls:
- Start with a single non-prod tenant and progressively widen to canary tenants before engaging low-priority prod.
- Circuit-breaker default thresholds will be halved for drill runs unless explicit approval from runtime lead.
- All changes are behind feature flags with automatic timeout rollback.

Open decisions (to finalize before dry-run):
- Thresholds for automatic promotion vs. manual approval (proposal: auto-promote when open_rate>10% sustained and promotion_time_simulated < 60s).
- Whether KV reconciliation should be synchronous during promotion or batched post-promotion (proposal: asynchronous converge with reconciliation window 15m).

Deliverables and timeline:
- Week 1: finalize runbook and circuit-breaker param matrix.
- Week 2: run isolated backup-restore validation and KV auditor baseline.
- Week 3: execute staged dry-run with canary tenants.
- Week 4: full scheduled drill with stakeholder sign-off and postmortem.

Acceptance: ticket marked Done when runbook merged, dry-run completed and signed off, KV-auditor merged, and drill postmortem posted.
